To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the harmonic mean estimator is the best among the estimators that are based on the augmented population; 2) if the plants are not captured, the best estimator is the harmonic mean estimator; 3) if the plants do not move, the best estimator among those that use the augmented population is the harmonic mean; 4) if the plants move, the best among the above estimators is the harmonic mean.
the harmonic mean is a robust, efficient and unbiased estimator of population size, which is improved by the addition of plants.
the use of plant captures can be useful in estimating population size in a continuous time framework, and that the performance of estimators can be improved by using plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of the size of a population of animals that cannot easily be observed.
the use of planted populations for estimating the abundance of target populations.
a method for estimating the size of an unknown population by means of a known planted population, which is added to the unknown population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the case of Poisson sighting processes, the use of planted individuals is beneficial, but the use of the harmonic mean estimator is more beneficial still.

the performance of the harmonic mean estimator is robust to the presence of a small number of individuals with a different intensity function, provided that the number of plants is sufficiently large, but that this estimator performs poorly when the intensity function of plants differs markedly from that of individuals in the target population, and when the number of plants added is small.
the performance of the harmonic mean estimator is robust to departures from the model assumptions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a plant-capture approach is a good way to improve the precision of population size estimation, and the harmonic mean estimator is the best of the estimators considered.
, in general, the harmonic mean estimator outperforms other estimators.
, for the plant-capture method, the performance of the harmonic mean estimator is robust to the presence of plants whose capture rates differ from those of individuals in the target population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the harmonic mean is a good choice for population size estimation, even if the plants have a different intensity function from the target population.
a plant-capture approach can be used to estimate the abundance of a target population in continuous time, provided that the intensity function of plants is known or estimable.
the use of a planted population can be beneficial in the estimation of the size of a target population.
